# [🔓 Open]{.status-open} Lower bounds for nonlinear Pauli estimation [#2]{.issue-number}

::: {.issue-meta}
[theory]{.label .label-bug} [priority: high]{.label .label-enhancement}
:::
:::

::: {.post-body}
## Motivation

Siyuan gave a 4-replica protocol that drops the $\mathcal{P}$-local constraint, achieving sample complexity $O(\log|\mathcal{P}|)$ with a highly nonlocal and adaptive circuit. We want to prove this is **optimal** by ruling out 2-replica and 3-replica possibilities.

## Problem Statement

For a fixed set of Pauli observables $P \in \mathcal{P}$, prove estimation lower and upper bounds on $\{\mathrm{Tr}[P\rho^2] : P \in \mathcal{P}\}$.

### Known Results

| Setting | Complexity | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Naive upper bound (local 2-replica per $P$) | $O(|\mathcal{P}|)$ | Issue #3 |
| Siyuan's 4-replica (nonlocal, adaptive) | $O(\log|\mathcal{P}|)$ | — |

### Goals

1. **Rule out 3-replica**: Show that no 3-replica protocol (local or nonlocal) can achieve $O(\log|\mathcal{P}|)$ sample complexity.
2. **Rule out 2-replica**: Show that no 2-replica protocol can achieve $O(\log|\mathcal{P}|)$ sample complexity.
3. Thereby establish $\Omega(\log|\mathcal{P}|)$ as tight, proving optimality of the 4-replica protocol.

### Relation to Prior Work

This generalizes ["Optimal tradeoffs for estimating Pauli observables"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19105) to the **nonlinear** ($\mathrm{Tr}[P\rho^2]$) setting.
:::
